standard_prerequisites.name: n-connected maps
standard_prerequisites.statement: f : A -> B is n-connected if trunc n (fiber_f b) is contractible for every b : B.
standard_prerequisites.use: The goal after the group-theoretic hypotheses are used is exactly the contractibility of trunc n (fiber_f b) for all b : B.

standard_prerequisites.name: The long exact sequence of a fibration
standard_prerequisites.statement: A fiber sequence gives a long exact sequence of homotopy groups, so vanishing and surjectivity statements about pi_k translate into statements about the fiber.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is applied at source line 2474 to deduce pi_k(fiber) = 0 for k <= n and contractibility of trunc 0 (fiber).

standard_prerequisites.name: Truncation does not change low homotopy groups
standard_prerequisites.statement: pi_k(trunc n X) = pi_k(X) for k <= n, and trunc n X is n-connected.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the passage at source line 2477 that turns the group information into contractibility via the Whitehead criterion.

core_obligations: Record that the forward direction is the earlier statement about the homotopy groups of an n-connected map (source line 2473).
For the converse, apply the long exact sequence of the fibration to conclude that pi_k(fiber_f(f(a))) = 0 for all k <= n and that trunc 0 (fiber_f(f(a))) is contractible (source lines 2474-2476).

Since pi_k(fiber) = pi_k(trunc n fiber) for k <= n and trunc n fiber is n-connected, apply the Whitehead criterion to conclude that trunc n (fiber_f(f(a))) is contractible for every a : A (source line 2477).

Extend from basepoints of the form f(a) to an arbitrary b : B: take x : trunc 0 A with |b|_0 = trunc 0 f (x) by the first hypothesis, use that contractibility is a mere proposition to assume x = |a|_0, and again to replace b by f(a) (source lines 2479-2482).

proof_roadmap.step: Dispose of the forward direction by the cited result.
Use the long exact sequence and the Whitehead criterion to get contractibility of the truncated fibers over the image of f.
Transport from the image to all of B using surjectivity on truncations and the fact that contractibility is a mere proposition.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Corollary 8.8.5 at source lines 2464-2471: for n >= 0 a map f : A -> B is n-connected if and only if trunc 0 f is an isomorphism, pi_k(f) is an isomorphism for k <= n and pi_{n+1}(f) is surjective. The converse direction, which is the substance of the proof (source lines 2472-2483), is not formal: one first has to feed the group-theoretic hypotheses into the long exact sequence of the fibration to learn that the fiber has vanishing homotopy groups up to n and contractible 0-truncation (lines 2474-2476), then convert that into contractibility of trunc n of the fiber over points of the form f(a) by the Whitehead criterion (line 2477), and finally extend to an arbitrary b : B by a two-step argument in which surjectivity of trunc 0 f provides a preimage in the truncation and the fact that contractibility is a mere proposition allows the truncations to be stripped twice (lines 2479-2482).
